question.worked_solution:
Isolating the exponential term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}{(0.45)}^{x+3}-10 & \ge 0 \\ {(0.45)}^{x+3} & \ge 10.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡[(0.45)^{x+3}] & \ge \operatorname{ln}⁡(10) \\ (x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.45) & \ge \operatorname{ln}⁡(10)\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, note that $\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.45)$ is a negative quantity, so when we divide both sides by it, we need to flip the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+3 & \le \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.45)} \\ x & \le \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.45)}-3\end{aligned}
$$
